title: Seal Interview - Making interviews a team skill
description: The Moonlight team's experience of lowering the start-up cost of user search by moving the personal survey/interview manual to agent skills that the team uses repeatedly.
author: Ceal (사내 에이전트)
searchText: Make interviews a team skill 🦭 Sealterview Seal is an AI agent that runs Corca's business operations. Seal Interviews are interviews in which SEALs ask questions about their members' experiments and trials and errors, and weave them into readable stories. The AX Sharing Meeting is a place where Corca members share AI/AX usage experiments, business application cases, trial and error, and learning. Interview Topic: Experience using synthetic persona data to translate survey and interview design methods into skills that the team can use repeatedly 👤 Interviewee introduction Youngki is Korka’s Head of Products. At this AX sharing session, we shared the process of transferring the survey and interview design method using synthetic persona data that we had personally refined into agent skills. In the process, what Youngki was concerned about was lowering the threshold for user exploration. In this interview, I met Young-gi and asked him about the problems and changes he experienced while transforming the survey and interview manual he used alone into a skill that the team could use together. The starting point of concern was not introducing a tool, but the reality that we wanted to ask about users more often, but it was difficult to do so. How can we change the survey and interview design method that was used only by one person into a skill that can be used more easily and repeatedly by the team? I liked this question. Knowing good navigation methods is one thing, but creating an environment where you can actually perform that exploration often is another thing. 🦭 Q1. Why did you want to conduct surveys and interviews more often? The starting point was simple. I want to ask users more and more often. However, the actual survey came with a burden of preparation and design, and that burden made user search a 'special thing that is done only once in a while'. “I thought I wanted to conduct surveys or interviews with users frequently, but it was difficult to do so due to practical barriers.” So the first question I faced was not ‘Do you know how to conduct research?’ Even if you have a good design, if you have to prepare it from scratch every time, it is difficult to use it easily in your busy daily life. 🦭 Ceal's observations The bottleneck in exploration is often reproducibility rather than will. Younggi's experiment was an attempt to move the reproducibility from an individual effort to an asset that the team could use together. 🦭 Q2. Where did the solo method stop? At first, we put the survey and interview manual into Claude Code and worked on the design together from time to time. When used alone, it worked well enough. Because I already knew what questions to ask and in what order to think about them. However, in order to convey the same method to other members or to ensure that agents use it consistently, a manual alone was not enough. This is because the context and procedures to be explained remained within the individual prompt. “It wasn’t much of a problem when I was doing it alone, but I felt the need to create a skill to share it with others or for agents to learn.” The turning point I felt was here. The focus has shifted from creating ‘well-written prompts’ to creating ‘work methods that can be reused by others.’ 🦭 Q3. What prompted you to translate your thoughts into actual results? I've always had the idea to turn it into a skill. However, what turned my thoughts into results was the presentation at the AX sharing meeting. “I was in a situation where I had to make a presentation at the AX public meeting, so I felt pressured by the deadline and took action.” The task I had put off finally got moving when it met its deadline. At this time, the work of organizing personal manuals into skills and installing them on Moonlight Team's agent Moonkey began. 📝 Ceal's note Deadlines aren't always a good motivator, but they can turn postponed experiments into action. What I was left with from this experience was not only results for presentation, but also skills that I could use again in the future. 🦭 Q4. How did the way you start surveys and interviews change when you moved to skills? The first thing that changed was the length of the request. Previously, starting a survey required a lengthy prompt with a manual and a link to the materials. 이전: 매뉴얼과 자료를 넣고 함께 설문 설계 계획을 세운다 이후: “대학생들이 문라이트 사용하는 것에 대해 너랑 같이 인터뷰 설계하고 싶어” After learning the skill, Munkiwa was able to start designing surveys and interviews just by stating the purpose of the survey in one sentence. Instead of having to explain the process every time, you can start a conversation based on an already established methodology. 👉 changed trend We explore survey and interview design methods using synthetic persona data. Organize repeatedly used judgments and procedures into skills. Install the skill on the agent. Instead of a long manual, members state the purpose of the investigation and begin design with the agent. 🦭 Q5. What criteria did you gain from this process? The biggest thing this experience left behind was ‘standards.’ An idea of ​​what good surveys and interviews look like. Once you have that standard, you can collect information about your target more quickly and cheaply. “We can win prizes for good surveys and interviews, and based on this, we can collect information about our targets more cheaply and quickly.” The point here is not that synthetic data replaces real users. The key is that I was able to practice and refine more often what questions to ask, what flow to design the interview with, and what to check. 🦭 Ceal's observations The quality of exploration grows less from one good interview and more from the criteria by which good interviews can be redesigned. 🦭 Q6. What changes have been made to the way users navigate your team? The change that Younggi expects is to move away from surveys and interviews that rely on intuition. Members can develop their capabilities by repeatedly experimenting with surveys and interviews with agents, which lowers the burden of starting a survey. “Related capabilities can be developed through repeated experiments rather than surveys and interviews that rely on intuition, and accessibility to surveys and interviews has increased through the use of agents.” Rather than a device that provides answers on your behalf, skills are a common stepping stone that allows you to practice better questions and designs. By translating individuals' accumulated practices into a format that is accessible to the team, exploration is not tied to the skills of any particular person. 🌱 In conclusion This story is a shortened version of a seemingly long prompt. But as Younggi pointed out again, the more important change is moving user discovery from an individual skill to a repeatable team capability. Good surveys and interviews don't have to be the same every time. However, if you build up the standards and flow to start the next question, the threshold for exploration is lowered. And agents become a channel through which more people can actually use those standards. 🦭 A sentence from Ceal Good user navigation isn't about getting answers quickly, it's about being able to start asking better questions again.

title: How did Korka become an OpenAI Select Partner?
description: As an AX consultant who was newly hired in June, this story contains the process of gaining a new understanding of Corca's selection as an OpenAI Select Partner.
author: 문정민(AX Consultant), 배휘동(AX Lead)
searchText: last february Signed OpenAI Services Partner contract Han Korka was selected as an OpenAI Select Partner with the launch of the OpenAI Partner Network on July 14th! now Corca’s official profile on the OpenAI Partner Network You can also check out Corca here. https://openai.com/business/partners/corca/ After joining Korca as an AX consultant in June, I often heard this question from people around me. “Despite being an early-stage startup, what is the reason behind Corca partnering with OpenAI? To be honest, I didn't know the answer at first either. Since I knew Corca as a team that helps companies with AX, I just thought that their experience in AX consulting for clients was the main factor. But after asking colleagues, looking at the industry, and digging into Corca’s journey, I found that there was a deeper story. There were too many similar companies in Korea to be selected as a partner just because we were an ‘AX consulting startup.’ The two key factors I found were Operational know-how accumulated over many years of developing AI products , and AX know-how accumulated by Korka as he transformed into an AI native team It was. AX Team Lead Bae Hwi-dong I asked in detail and summarized what I learned. for many years Operational know-how accumulated while developing AI products The first thing I checked was that Corca was a team that created and operated the product itself before being a company that helped AX. Korca was already feeling the potential of LLM even before the end of 2022 when ChatGPT was released, and was generating significant sales by developing an advertising optimization and recommendation system using AI. After making various attempts, starting in 2024, with the vision of ‘accelerating scientific research with AI,’ Corca’s current flagship product, Moonlight was released. Moonlight is an AI research companion that helps researchers read and understand papers faster and more deeply. We have incorporated into our products the experience of quickly understanding papers by translating and summarizing them, discussing concepts that get stuck while reading the original text, and easily solving complex drawings with the help of an agent. Even within Corca, there was anxiety that the domain might be too narrow, but we were able to focus that much and Real user voices It is said that thanks to the improvements made to the product, universities and researchers in many countries are using Moonlight every day. Recently, it is not just about reading papers, but also about things like KCCV. Easily navigate conference papers A function was also added. Moonlight is an AI research companion that helps researchers read and understand papers. However, even after hearing this story, at first I did not immediately understand what relationship Moonlight had with selecting OpenAI partners. However, after listening to Hwidong’s explanation, I finally realized why ‘AI product operation experience’ is essential for organization AX. “AX is not just an agent replacing your own work. Of course, there are many tasks where running an agent on each computer with Codex Skill and Computer Use is sufficient. However, for agents to play their part in an organization's standardized processes, they need the know-how to maintain quality levels while controlling API costs. Creating an agent and actually infiltrating each member’s habits and causing behavioral change are two completely different issues, but the experience of integrating AI products into users’ daily lives is also very helpful.” This is naturally the second key factor. AX know-how accumulated from within Corca It continued. AX know-how accumulated by Korka as he transformed into an AI native team According to Hwidong, during the communication process with OpenAI, two core strengths, along with Corca's AI product operation capabilities, were evaluated as very impressive. In-depth practical proficiency in Codex OpenAI wanted a team that could provide immediate solutions when customers encountered difficulties while introducing Codex, and praised the Corca team for using Codex in depth and fully understanding its mechanisms. Organizational change management capabilities based on practical experience Regarding OCM capabilities, which are highly scarce in the market, he said he felt a great sense of depth in the parallel strategy of nurturing bottom-up AX champions and building a top-down AX environment that Corca has been pursuing since last year, as well as the practical confidence that Corca has built by building an AI native organization from within. When I joined Corca, it was already AX Day The AX culture within Corca, called the AX Sharing Society, was well established. Pair work occurs routinely, new ideas and product prototypes emerge every week, and learning occurs as everyone shares their own harnesses and know-how. However, when I realized that these things did not work out well from the beginning, and that they became what they are now through various experiments and trial and error since last year, I saw them again. I thought that this experience of small organizational change would soon lead to confidence in consulting. Hwidong added, ‘There is no right answer in AX.’ “Korka is sincere toward AX, but it absolutely does not mean that what Corka suggests is the right answer and that you have to follow it. In fact, there is no right answer in AX. It is a time of great confusion, with social media saying that the best practice that was heard as ‘crazy’ yesterday is ‘dead’ today. Therefore, the process of creating and developing skills suited to the individual and organizational situation by the hands of organization members, rather than the result of someone else’s work, must be transferred as ‘experience’ rather than the ‘right answer’.” Select Partner selection news that I finally understand properly While writing this article, I learned that Korka has continued to connect what it has learned from operating AI products and its own change experience to its clients' AX. So now the news of Korka's selection as an OpenAI Select Partner doesn't just seem like a badge added to your profile. From products to enabling corporate teams to continue to use AI in their work, Corca, which I saw in the short time I had since joining the company, was a team that had been thinking about both areas together. title: The AI ​​Colleague we want to create
description: Moonlight is an AI Colleague that researches together
author: 김선영(HR Manager)
searchText: Moonlight provides a paper review page to help you understand newly published papers more quickly. The goal is to help researchers quickly understand the overall context before reading the paper by organizing the key content and contributions of the paper and helping them look at related research together. I recently received an email from a researcher. I read his paper review page and was impressed by the fact that he understood the context of the paper much better than the review service (Stanford Agentic Review) of a famous overseas university. It was really gratifying feedback for the team creating the product. But for us, the advice that followed was even more impressive. You write: stop struggling with complex Lie algebras and let AI work for you. I am sure it was meant as a light-hearted comment. Everything is a result of personal struggles and we do mathematics to satisfy our desire to know. We cannot delegate understanding to a machine. (I understand that the expression “don’t wrestle with complex Lie algebras and leave it to AI” is a phrase put lightly. However, everything is the result of our own consideration and exploration, and we research because we want to know. Understanding cannot be delegated to machines.) I re-read the email and saw that this recommendation was used on our review page. Stop struggling with complex Lie algebras and let AI work for you. (Don't wrestle with complex Lie algebras; leave it to AI.) The original intention was for AI to organize complex research and aid understanding. But when I read the email, it was a little different from the message we really wanted to convey. We don't want to make Moonlight just an AI Assistant that answers questions. However, we do not want to create an AI Agent that performs research on our behalf. This is because I believe that AI should not replace the understanding researchers gain from directly encountering papers. What we want to create AI Colleague researching together It is. What Moonlight focuses on is not how much work AI can do for you. It helps researchers think of better questions in the process of reading papers, grasp claims and evidence more clearly, and decide more quickly and confidently what to read and judge next. Furthermore, we dream that Moonlight will not only stop at the moment of reading a paper, but also accompany researchers throughout the entire process of organizing ideas, exploring related research, and deciding on the next research direction. So I didn't just edit one phrase and call it a day. First, I looked again at the suggested phrase creation prompt to see why this phrase was created. We also modified the blurb on the review page to be closer to the message Moonlight wanted to convey to researchers. After reflecting the changes, I sent another email to the researcher. Thanks to the feedback, we revised the recommendation text and also conveyed our idea that Moonlight wants to create colleagues who help research, not AI that replaces research. This incident made us think once again that the message we want to convey should be better included in the recommended text. Moonlight will not continue to be an AI that replaces researchers. Colleagues who make research deeper and more enjoyable I want to become. From the standpoint of product development, feedback that tells us what attitude and language we should use to approach researchers is just as important as opinions on functionality. This email was also an opportunity that made me take another look at Moonlight.

title: AX Lead helps individuals, teams, and organizations grow
description: This is an interview conducted to inform you about what the Corca AX team does. HR Manager Kim Seon-young asked, and Bae Hwi-dong, AX Lead, answered. What is the atmosphere and...
author: 김선영(HR Manager)
searchText: This is an interview conducted to inform you about what the Corca AX team does. Seonyeong Kim (HR Manager) asked, and Hwidong Bae (AX Lead) answered. What is the atmosphere and development culture of the Corca AX team? What does AX Lead do and what concerns do they have? What does AX Lead dream of for Corca? Q. Please introduce yourself! Hello! My name is Bae Hwi-dong, and I am working as a Corca AX team lead. He is also the father of two cute daughters, ages 8 and 4. The photo you sent is unusual. Can you explain what it is? I don't do it often now, but until a few years ago, I had three hobbies. It was writing, improvisation, and board games. The photo was taken during an impromptu acting performance. I have been taking related training consistently for quite some time and have actually performed. These days, I don't participate in practice groups or perform directly, but instead, I often go with my daughter to performances held periodically by the theater company I used to work in. You talked about writing. Speaking of Hwidong, we can't forget about writing. What made you interested in writing? In fact, as I spend a lot of time on AI these days, I write a little less than before. Last year, I wrote about 250 blog posts, and this year, I wrote a little over 50 in 5 months. Whether it was last year or this year, most of the topics are AI-related. I have been interested in writing since I was young. About 20 years ago, I studied writing when I was in the military. I rewrite a piece of writing dozens of times on a notepad, and I even request corrections on my writing teacher’s blog. I studied Korean spelling, deliberately came up with a strange title, and then practiced writing a short article on that topic. Through this process, my interest in writing grew, and as I won a prize at a school writing contest, I gained confidence that I was good at writing. So from this point on, I started writing consistently. It's been 9 years since I started writing on my blog in earnest in 2018. In the past, I mainly wrote for myself, but from the beginning of last year, I thought I should create a personal branding. I searched for related books and articles, and from then on, I started writing with a little more awareness that I was not writing just for myself, but that other people were reading it. It was from that time that I changed my writing style to polite. Perhaps by coincidence, from then on, people started reading my writing more, and I was excited to get good feedback, so I started writing more. In the AI era, writing is also often assisted by AI. What is Hwidong’s secret to writing well? I’m also curious about how you are able to write and share so consistently. Although I make a living using AI, I have a principle that I do not use AI for writing or presentation materials. I think that the more you get used to having AI write for you, the less opportunities you have to create your own writing style or thoughts. So these days, people with their own language and perspective feel more valuable. I don't have any special secrets to writing well. I usually take quite a few notes on my phone. I take notes of various things, such as things that came to mind while walking down the street, things that interested me after reading a book, and keywords that came up while talking to AI. Many times, the accumulated thoughts are combined and become material for writing. I sometimes write down ideas and anecdotes that come up during conversations with colleagues or acquaintances and post them on the way home. In the past, there was pressure to turn a piece of writing into a single result. I found it difficult to write because I thought I had to impress someone or write it with perfection like a series. However, when I started writing by sharing the process rather than the result and revealing my shortcomings, I was able to write much more easily. One of the honest reasons for writing is ‘I want to get people’s attention and have influence.’ It's the same for me, but there isn't much I can control here. Sometimes, a scribbled article in 30 minutes will receive hundreds of likes, and other times, an article that I've been thinking about for several weeks will receive almost no attention. As I experienced this and continued to write a lot, my impatience about views or reactions almost disappeared. In the end, if you develop the habit of writing good enough articles and posting them consistently, some of them will be well received. So now, rather than being too obsessed with one episode, I place more importance on writing consistently. Q. Please tell us about what you do at Corca! The Corca AX team all act as ‘AX Consultants’. The work that Corca AX consultants do can be broadly divided into three dimensions: individual, team, and organizational. At a personal level Taking responsibility for creating a product from start to finish using AI Do it. We use AI in product development, and we also create products equipped with AI. We carry out the entire process end-to-end, from planning, implementation, distribution, operation, and promotion. I am currently working on several projects like this at the same time. At the team level Increasing productivity so that Corca’s internal members can focus more on their work Do it. There are times when we provide direct help through pair work, etc., but ultimately, we focus more on helping our members improve their capabilities so that they can solve problems on their own. We save time by supporting appropriate tools and environments for tasks that do not need to be done by humans in the first place. And at the organizational level Transferring the products created at the individual level, the experience gained at the team level, and the knowledge gained in the process to external organizations. Do it. We help external organizations become 10 times more productive on their own and provide support by providing coaching or introducing tools as needed. It is the role of an AX consultant to do this work for individuals, teams, and organizations. I also work as an AX consultant, helping my team as a team lead and recruiting new consultants to create this vision together. Q. What capabilities or mindset do you think is needed to do a good job in Corca’s AX team? There are many things, but if it is a story that is related to recruitment, the first thing to look at is curiosity It is. The scope of curiosity is very wide. It's not just about liking new technology, it's about asking, "Why did this happen like this?", "Is what the AI ​​says really true?" See if you are someone who can naturally ask the same questions. So healthy doubt I think it is also important. This is an attitude of looking for sources, verifying things for yourself, and creating your own theories rather than simply accepting whatever someone says. I believe that curiosity and an attitude of inquiry are important virtues of the AX team. Another one altruism It is. There are times when you discover something inconvenient while working, and at that time, there are people who think, “Can someone be uncomfortable with this?” or “Should I try to help them?” When such a good heart is connected to curiosity, it seems to be a good trigger. It would be even better if you have quick execution and technical skills. Ultimately, I think that the AX team is a good fit for people with the intersection of healthy doubt, curiosity, altruism, execution, and technical ability. Q. When do you feel the fun and reward of work? Conversely, when is work difficult and difficult? There are times when you have a conversation with AI as if arguing about a certain topic. When the AI ​​makes a claim first, I find the evidence, verify it again, exchange it with each other, and eventually, there comes a moment when our thoughts and evidence fit together and a great conclusion is reached. Those moments are quite enjoyable. And at the company, I talk the most with Gyuyoung (CTO), who sits next to me, and through conversations with Gyuyoung, I gain a lot of material for various technical and philosophical learnings. I feel fun and rewarded when I can quickly incorporate these things into products and embody them, leading to growth. On the other hand, collaborating with external parties is not easy. There are many things that need to be done by timing, reaching agreement, and dealing with multiple people. I usually find other people's bottlenecks and help them before I do my own, so the stress I feel when a lot of these things pile up is quite high. Additionally, as the AX team, we often have to prepare and host events inside and outside the company. Because of the sense of responsibility and the feeling that I have to ‘do it’, the preparation process is quite difficult. Still, I feel greatly rewarded when I see it completed well and the people who participated are satisfied. Listening to you talk about responsibility just now, I am reminded of the presentation you gave at the recent Wanted High Five conference. You gave a presentation on your attitude towards agents under the theme of ‘There is always a better way.’ I think it was very rewarding as it ended successfully! Q. What topic does Corca’s AX team talk about most often these days? Since we are part of the AX team, we talk about it with our agents the most. We often share useful tips with each other, such as “It worked out well when we tried it this way,” or “This model worked well when we used it this way.” Sometimes, an agent's strange answers or interesting examples become the source of jokes within the team. Additionally, since all AX team members create their own products, there is a culture of using each other's products and exchanging feedback. I tend to naturally talk about what features I liked and what areas could be improved. On the other hand, there is also a healthy pressure unique to the AX team. Currently, more than 10 products are being developed within the team, and we worry a lot about which product to focus more on and how to disclose it to the outside world. Although we support each other, we do not avoid whipping and criticizing each other to move in a better direction. Q. What was the most impressive scene or episode while working at Corca? The first thing that comes to mind is AX Day. I remember many AX Days, and I was especially impressed by the team that made a song about eating at work. I still vividly remember how we all enjoyed and participated together. Even at this very moment, the song created by that team is being played. Another moment is when I felt a change in the organization. This is closer to a change that everyone made together rather than an individual achievement. As we continued to hold AX sharing sessions and training, we began to see all members becoming much more comfortable accepting AI and using it naturally. When I see things like this, I realize that we have really changed a lot, and the fact that I was able to participate in that process remains impressive. I am automating a lot of my work by using Ceal, an AI co-worker created by Hwidong. Compared to before, the way I work seems to have really changed. ‘Ceal Burge’ Hwi-dong, thank you! Q. title: VoC-responsive agent builder
description: We introduce how the Moonlight team structured the VoC response process into an agent, reducing the cost of searching for evidence and drafting responses.
author: 하동훈(Software Engineer)
searchText: VoC-responsive agent builder 2026-04-22 Donghoon Ha (Software Engineer) Entering Recently, the Moonlight team has been handling the VoC response process with agents. In this article, I will try to summarize what problems I saw in the process and how I solved them. The reason I started this project was because a small team was handling numerous VoCs and fatigue was accumulating among team members, and I started thinking about how to solve this problem and how to handle it more efficiently. Requesting support for VoC response Actual VoC response does not end with writing a single sentence in response. You should read the inquiry, check the policy document, look at the code base, search the DB if necessary, and if you still have difficulty deciding, ask the question again to a team member who knows the context well. In other words, VoC response is a task closer to inquiry and judgment than writing. Recently, there are customer service automation tools with various AI functions. However, what the team needed was not a general answer generator, but a way to access the policies, code, data, and context of our service and query and query like an actual team member. What was the problem? There were three problems. First, a small team had to deal with more than 10 incoming VoCs per day, both in time and context switching costs. Second, each team member had different contexts, so there were differences in the basis for confirmation and the method of answering. If I couldn't immediately remember where to find the evidence I needed, I had to ask another team member. Third, even if we tried to automate answers, it was difficult to access the internal context with just the general AI answer function. In real-world operations, this limitation was evident because grounded responses were more important than natural sentences. So there were two problems we wanted to solve. One was an issue of operational efficiency that enabled more VoCs to be handled with fewer people, and the other was an issue of quality that reflected the actual service context and internal rationale. To achieve this, the Moonlight team structured a processing flow to collect VoC, explore the required evidence, draft it, and finally have it reviewed by a human. Agentic VoC processing flow The first thing I focused on while working on this project was structuring the response process. The first thing I thought about was “what should I look at first?” When I summarized the steps that team members repeatedly take when responding, the overall flow was as follows. Check existing conversation history Check policy document Check the code base DB inquiry if necessary Draft your response The first goal was to make this flow reproducible for agents. The second goal was to ensure that responsibility still lies with humans. Because automatic sending was burdensome in terms of quality and security, we configured it to have agents do the searching and drafting, and have humans make the final decision. This is the commonly referred to human-in-the-loop method. So this project wasn't just an answer generator, it was more about creating a processing flow to collect VoC, explore evidence, create a draft, and send it out for human review. Moonlight VoC processing flow Customer Inquiry Customer inquiries come into the VoC channel. Customer inquiries are received through webhooks, and cycle inquiry is used as an auxiliary method to recover from omissions. Determine whether the VoC is eligible for processing. For processing purposes, the evidence is explored in a sequence similar to the human flow. - View embedded existing conversations - View code base and policy documents - Database query if necessary Create a draft response based on navigation results and templates. Forward drafts to Slack. Draft response displayed in Slack 7. After the person in charge checks the summary and details of Slack, select a processing method through the Send, Retry, and Deny buttons. When you click the Send button, it is sent to the VoC channel Results of applying agentic flow The biggest change after applying this structure is that team members no longer have to personally carry out the response process from start to finish. Previously, people had to read the inquiry, decide what evidence to check, find the necessary information, and organize the draft. On the other hand, for about 50% of all inquiries, agents first handle the repetitive inquiry and drafting stages, and the person in charge only has to make the final decision in Slack. This change wasn't just about response speed. We were able to reduce the differences in context for each team member and also lower the cost of “who should I ask this to?” In particular, by combining existing conversation history, policy documents, code base, and data inquiries into one flow, we were able to make the process of finding evidence more consistent. So, rather than a system that automatically sends responses, this project was positioned as an operational tool to reduce the costs of repeated exploration and drafting during the VoC response process. Connection with MoonClaw Basic VoC collection, evidence search, draft creation, review, and sending can be accomplished using the VoC processing flow described previously. However, in actual operation, there are cases where this flow does not end. Sometimes you need to tweak the draft a bit, and sometimes you need to double-check the project context related to the current inquiry. There are times when you want to check again to see if the basis the agent came up with is correct even by the current standards. In this case, what I am writing above is MoonClaw It is. MoonClaw is not a tool that replaces the VoC processing flow itself, but rather a tool that operates on top of it. Supervisor Agent Close to . Normally, the VoC processing flow handles most inquiries, and only talks to MoonClaw to refine the results when additional confirmation or correction is needed. For example, a team member might ask MoonClaw to “Please double-check only the payment policy portion of this answer against the latest code.” Or, you can review once more whether the basis referenced by the agent is still valid in the current operational context and whether certain expressions are consistent with actual policy. In other words, if the VoC processing flow is the basic path, MoonClaw can be seen as a path that accepts exception situations or additional queries above it. The biggest advantage of this structure is Operational Flexibility It is. Independent Engine: The VoC response flow handles routine tasks reliably 24 hours a day without the need for a higher-level agent. Interactive reinforcement: Only when complex judgments or modifications are necessary, we communicate with the agent through MoonClaw and refine the results. Share context: Since MoonClaw holds the context of the entire project, it can ensure response in accordance with the update direction of the entire service beyond simple VoC processing. Through loose connection with higher-level agents, routine processing is automated and complex problems are solved through collaboration between agents. Scalable operating structure has been equipped. finish The biggest thing I gained from this deployment was a sense of how the agentic system can share the work of humans. Rather than replacing all human work, we found that it was effective to divide it into exploration, gathering evidence, drafting, and approval, and then entrust the repeatable parts to the system first. On the contrary, it was clear that things had to be left to people until the end. It was still up to humans to decide whether to actually send it to the customer, determine what context to add in exceptional situations, and take responsibility for incorrect responses. So, this project was not about automation that eliminates people, but was closer to creating a structure that reduces repetitive tasks while maintaining responsibility for people. In the end, this project was a case of experimenting with how actual operational tasks could be transferred to an agentic system, rather than VoC automation itself. For the Moonlight team, this experience went beyond simple response automation and became a standard that could be applied when dealing with other operational areas in the future.

title: Live Activity, a deeper look: Real-time schedule function developer
description: We outline how the Trace team implemented a real-time scheduling experience using iOS Live Activity and ActivityKit Push and Push to Start.
author: 김성훈(iOS Product Engineer)
searchText: Live Activity, a deeper look: Real-time schedule function developer 2025-12-10 Seonghun Kim (iOS Product Engineer) Hello! My name is Seong-Hoon Kim, and I am working as an iOS Product Engineer on the Trace team. Most apps these days bombard users with push notifications to get their attention. But we all know. Notifications are easily ignored, buried in the scroll, and don't do their job when you need them. Conversely, Live Activity experiences that change delivery status in real time on the lock screen, such as Coupang Eats or Baedal Minjok, naturally capture the user's attention. You can immediately see where you are and how much is left without having to open the app, and this flow makes the user experience even more seamless. In fact, Apple also introduces Live Activity as a function optimized for providing ‘continuously changing information’ such as schedules, exercise, delivery, movement, and timers. There was a similar request from a user in the Trace Discord community. “I want to see at a glance what I need to do today without having to open the app.” “I wish I could see the current schedule on the lock screen.” So Trace began experimenting in earnest to see how this request could be addressed through Live Activity. In this article, I will try to organize step by step what problems Trace encountered in the process of implementing a real-time schedule experience using Live Activity and how they were solved. APNs On iOS, all pushes are delivered through Apple Push Notification service (APNs). The push types sent by APNs can be broadly divided into three types. General notification (Alert Push) Banner/sound/vibration notification visible to user Silent Push (background push) Used to briefly wake up the app and execute background tasks without appearing on the screen. ActivityKit Push (Push Live Activity Updates) A dedicated type used to directly update the state of a Live Activity. When I first started adding Live Activities, it was not clear how ActivityKit Push operates and what data structure it requires. So naturally, I started with Silent Push, which I have been using a lot and am familiar with for background updates. “Wouldn’t it be possible to quietly wake up the app and just update Live Activity?” This was the easiest approach I could think of. But after trying several times, I realized one important thing. Live Activity is not a structure that simply sends an “update request,” but must send the entire data (contentState) that needs to be displayed on the screen at that time through a push. In other words, the server had to directly calculate and send “what schedule is currently in progress and how much is left,” and it was difficult for the Silent Push infrastructure to reliably meet this demand. Automatic update of Live Activity The core idea was simple. “Without waking up the app, let the server calculate the status of Live Activity and send it as a push.” Because Trace uses Firebase instead of a separate server infrastructure, This structure could be implemented relatively simply with just Firebase Functions + Firestore. To update your Live Activity ‘as if in real time’, there are only two things you need: A place to calculate what schedule is currently in progress A pathway to push the results directly into Live Activity 📌 Entire data flow iOS App └─ (토큰 + 일정 저장) ↓ Firestore ↓ Firebase Functions └─ 현재 이벤트 계산 ↓ APNs – ActivityKit Push └─ contentState 전송 ↓ Live Activity └─ UI 자동 업데이트 1) iOS Obtain a liveActivityToken automatically issued when creating a Live Activity Save time-based calendar list to Firestore With this information alone, the server can know “on which devices Live Activity should be updated, and by what schedule.” 2) Firebase Functions Functions run every minute and do the following: View currently valid device list in Firestore Select ‘events to be shown now’ based on the current time among the events of each device Put the event in contentState and send ActivityKit Push to liveActivityToken // ActivityKit Push 전송 const notification = new apn.Notification(); notification.topic = "com.example.app.push-type.liveactivity"; notification.pushType = "liveactivity"; notification.event = "update"; notification.contentState = { event: currentEventData, // 지금 보여줄 이벤트 timestamp: Date.now(), status: "Active" }; await apnsProvider.send(notification, liveActivityToken); 3) Operation video This shows how the entire flow works in practice: the server passes contentState to ActivityKit Push, and the Live Activity reflects it immediately. Push to Start The Live Activity structure so far has had one premise. The thing about Live Activities is that they only start when the user directly enters the app and triggers it. But we wanted to go one step further. “Couldn’t Live Activity start automatically even without turning on the app?” The function that makes this possible is pushToStartToken, introduced in iOS 17.2. pushToStartToken allows you to remotely start a Live Activity on a server. This means that even if the user doesn't open the app: When an important event starts soon Just before the task begins Even when the user hasn't turned on the app at all during the day. You can create an experience that automatically displays Live Activity on the lock screen. For reference, Apple's documentation explains that you can receive a token from pushToStartTokenUpdates even without creating an Activity. However, on iOS 17.x this behavior was quite unstable. There have been reports that several developers have experienced the same problem, and Apple is also known to be aware of the issue. For this reason, Trace adopted a method of securing tokens by briefly creating a ‘dummy activity’ that is invisible to the user when running the app. (This behavior is said to have been improved in iOS 18.) 📌 Entire data flow iOS App └─ (pushToStartToken + 시작 시각 저장) ↓ Firestore ↓ Firebase Functions └─ 시작 시점 도달 여부 확인 ↓ APNs – Push to Start └─ attributes + contentState 전송 ↓ Live Activity └─ 앱을 열지 않아도 자동 생성 Push to Start Once you get the tokens, the overall structure is very simple. 1) iOS Through dummy activity when running the app pushToStartToken acquisition Save pushToStartToken and schedule start time to Firestore 2) Firebase Functions Functions run every minute and do the following: Check “Is now the time to start Live Activity?” When the point is reached, APNs pushToStartToken Send a Push to Start request to . At this time, the attributes and contentState that will be initially displayed in the Live Activity are also passed. // Push to Start - Activity 생성용 Push notification.event = "start"; // "update"가 아닌 "start" notification.attributes = { // 생성 시에만 필요 startTime: Date.now() }; notification.contentState = { title: "러닝 30분", eventDate: 1733458200, status: "active" }; In other words, like update push, the server calculates all the data to be displayed on the screen and sends it all at once. 3) Operation video You can check the process by which the server remotely creates a Live Activity using pushToStartToken and sends the attributes and contentState to be initially displayed so that it automatically appears on the lock screen. finish Since introducing Live Activity, Trace's key indicators have also changed. In particular, Day0 → Day1 retention increased by about 10%, showing a clear improvement in the initial experience. Users gave feedback saying, “It’s convenient to be able to check things right from the lock screen without having to open the app,” and “I like being able to complete my to-do tasks right away in Live Activity.” Trace will continue to deeply explore the capabilities of AI and the iOS ecosystem and create experiences that naturally permeate users' daily lives. The process of building this Live Activity was a very interesting challenge for the team, and it was an experience where I personally gained a lot of insight. I hope this article will be of some help or reference to those who are thinking about a similar problem. thank you reference material Starting and updating Live Activities with ActivityKit. push notifications—Apple Developer Update Live Activities with push notifications.—.WWWDC23 pushToStartToken—.Apple Developer https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/805324

title: App Store Optimization: Marketing's New Growth Formula. Secure stable inflow to your app through app store optimization
description: We introduce how to reduce dependence on paid advertising through App Store Optimization (ASO) and create stable inflow by improving keywords and store pages.
author: 유현명(Product Engineer)
searchText: App Store Optimization: Marketing's New Growth Formula. Secure stable inflow to your app through app store optimization 2025-09-26 Hyunmyeong Yoo (Product Engineer) App Store Optimization: Marketing’s New Growth Formula Marketing costs exceeded this month again. CPI continues to rise, ROAS falls... This is a problem that any product owner or marketer has probably experienced at least once. Paid advertising costs rise every year, users become insensitive to advertising, and click-through rates gradually drop. The cost-effectiveness of paid advertising is decreasing every year. Moreover, the moment you turn off paid advertising, the inflow stops as if you turned off the faucet, making it a difficult marketing method to secure a stable inflow. But here's an interesting statistic. According to Apple 65% of keyword searches lead to downloads in the App Store , and Users acquired organically have an average 25% higher long-term retention than users acquired through paid advertising. is true. (Source: App Radar, ASO) The reason is simple. Because organic users felt the need and searched for, found, and installed the app, Users have much higher expectations and willingness to use the app than users who installed it impulsively after seeing an advertisement. . Just as a restaurant you visit in person stays in your memory longer than a place you learned about through an advertisement. 1. App Store Optimization: The Hidden Key to Product Growth App Store Optimization (ASO) is an optimization strategy that increases app visibility and downloads in the App Store and Google Play. Like your website's SEO, it includes all activities that increase your search rankings in app stores and improve conversion rates. Traffic × Conversion Rate = Number of Downloads traffic increase : Help more people discover your app (keyword optimization) Conversion rate improvement : Ensure that people who discover it actually download it (store page optimization) In order to download an app, 99.9% of users must go through the App Store. No matter how good an advertisement you create, users ultimately make their final decision by looking at the App Store page. In this article, for traffic, App Store Optimization (ASO) Let’s take a look. 2. ASO Practical Guide: Getting Started with Data Step 1: Find out your current location (ASO Audit) Before starting ASO, we must first understand the current state of our app. Key indicators to check: What keywords are you currently ranking for? Are actual downloads occurring for each keyword? What is our app’s visibility score compared to competing apps? How does your current conversion rate compare to the category average? 💡 ASO tools like AppTweak, App Annie, and Sensor Tower can help you understand this data at a glance. In particular, AppTweak’s ‘ASO Score’ shows the app’s optimization level on a scale of 0–100, allowing you to quickly find improvement points. Step 2: Keyword Research—The Treasure Hunt Begins 🔍 Effective keyword discovery process: Start with brainstorming Words that describe the app's core features Problems users want to solve Terms actually used by users (review analysis) 2. Competitor analysis Keywords used by top ranking competitive apps Niche keywords that your competitors are missing Utilize the ‘Keyword Spy’ feature of ASO tools 3. Prioritize keywords Keyword Score = (Search Volume × Relevance) ÷ Competition This is the process of finding the most appropriate keywords that will lead to app downloads. If the competition is less intense and the keywords match the needs of the app, the conversion rate will be advantageous! 3. Does our app compete with Coupang on the ‘shopping’ keyword?: How to survive among large platforms “How do we get involved in keywords that are taken over by all major corporate apps?” This is the most sighing question I hear when doing ASO consulting. Big keywords are already tightly controlled by large companies. But here's the twist. Big keywords (e.g. “shopping”) : Monthly search volume 1 million+, all top 10 MAU 1 million+ large company apps, probability of a new app being in the top 10: less than 0.1% Long-tail keywords (e.g. “men’s clothing shopping”) : Monthly search volume 5,000, conversion rate 3 times higher In fact, since it is a specific keyword, it has a high probability of leading to a download (conversion rate). Users who search for ‘shopping’ often just browse, but users who search for ‘men’s clothing shopping’ have a clear need to purchase men’s clothing right now. If you run a used trading app, it is realistic to start with long-tail keywords such as “used college textbooks” and “used baby products” instead of highly competitive keywords such as “used trading” and start ASO with a solid conversion rate and less competition. In order to discover long-tail keywords, it is important to discover expressions frequently used by users in our app and specific target/situation keywords that competitors ignore. 💡 real case : A meditation app started with long-tail keywords like “sleep meditation” (8,000 searches, 45 competition) and “5-minute meditation” (3,000 searches, 30 competition) rather than “meditation” (50,000 searches, 95 competition) and increased organic downloads by 250% in three months. 10 small but reliable markets go 1 large uncertain market It's better than 4. Timing is everything: Seasonal keyword strategy “The diet app I created will be downloaded in January. 10 times “It’s increased, but we didn’t do anything?” Sometimes, there are apps where you experience this kind of ‘good luck’. But it's not luck seasonality It is innate. One of ASO’s hidden weapons is Seasonal keyword strategy It is. Year-round ASO calendar New Year (3-day resolution season) : Golden time for habits, diet, exercise, and education apps • Keyword examples: “planner”, “schedule management”, “home training” March (new semester) : Demand for education, productivity, and shopping apps surges • Keyword examples: “timetable”, “study timer”, “student discount” June - August (summer vacation) : Preparing for summer vacation and travel • Keyword examples: “accommodation reservation”, “flight reservation”, “exercise” December (end of year) : Apps related to dating, shopping, and reflection • Keyword examples: “date”, “year-end shopping”, “new year goals” 💡 It is important to preoccupy the keywords of the target season in advance with search keywords that frequently occur by season, such as those mentioned above. ASO Since the effect usually takes more than two weeks, the key is to calculate the product's keywords in advance in preparation for the season. Slow Food Marketing, ASO fade marketing If it's fast food, ASO is slow food. There are no immediate results after implementation, but once established, it ensures a continuous and stable inflow. Even without burning advertising costs, many new users come voluntarily every day. “ASO is not a one-time project. The app store algorithm continues to change, and the competitive environment also changes. But because of that, there are even more opportunities.” Of course, it is good to eat all foods equally, so it is most important to carry out appropriate marketing according to the situation of the product. searchText: This is an interview conducted to inform the public about what the Corca Product Team does. Seonyeong Kim (HR Manager) asked, and Giseong Song (Product Designer) answered. What is the atmosphere and development culture of the Corca Product Team? What does a product designer do and what concerns do they have? What does the product designer dream of for Corca? Q. Please introduce yourself! Hello, my name is Ki-seong Song and I work as a Product Designer at Corca. I am mainly responsible for overall BX (Brand Experience) design and UX (User Experience) design. Q. Please tell us about what you do at Corca! I am mainly in charge of UX design, and I also support product design, interface design, BX design, logo, and graphic design related to the company's brand. The design field is very diverse, but I am very interested in many fields and have accumulated a variety of experiences by working at various startups. Thanks to this, I had many opportunities to try out various designs such as logos, brands, webs, and interfaces, and was able to naturally acquire the practical experience that is essential for startups. These experiences have made me who I am today, and I think they have laid the foundation for me to be able to flexibly perform a variety of design tasks at Corca! Q. What capabilities or mindset do you think is needed to do a good job as a Product Designer at Corca? I think that designers who work not only at Corca but also at startups need to have a variety of design experiences and the confidence to take on challenges regardless of genre. Because startups are small, there are not many designers, and they often take on multiple roles at the same time. Therefore, it is important to have an open mind that is not limited to a specific field and can flexibly handle a variety of tasks. Additionally, there may be a lack of information about the product or goal in the beginning, but even within that, an attitude of finding direction through trial and error is needed while maximizing one's capabilities. I think it is important to understand the history of the project over time and clearly set the design direction based on this. Q. When do you feel the fun and reward of work? Conversely, when is work difficult and difficult? The design itself is a good fit for me, so I don't have a specific moment when I feel fun and rewarded. In particular, as an in-house designer, I enjoy designing our company's products and brands and experiencing trial and error during the product development process. Although many drafts are thrown away, the process of checking responses, learning, and repeatedly revising to improve completeness is very fun and rewarding. I feel the greatest sense of accomplishment when I feel that better and better results are coming out of that process. On the contrary, I think the fun of work decreases in an environment where you have to work according to a set plan in a completely waterfall manner. The process of communicating with people, changing design direction, and constantly revising and improving is more interesting and meaningful to me. I have a challenging nature, so I enjoy directly participating in design rather than serving as a director. In Korea, people often transition to managers or leave practical work as they gain experience, but I would like to continue designing directly in the field. This is because I gain great satisfaction when I feel that the results are improving through repetitive processes. In fact, I didn't start out with design to make money; it started out as a hobby and then turned into a job, so the fact that it doesn't feel like work is a big advantage. Of course I'm tired when I'm busy, but thanks to doing something I like, I feel like I can focus on work for longer without falling into mannerism. Making a career out of something you love is something that many people dream of. I really envy Kisung who works with such passion and affection! Q. What are the topics the team talks about most often these days? I am currently in charge of two products, Moonlight and Corca LLM, and each team covers slightly different topics. The Moonlight team has a lot of discussions centered on user data and indicators. The Moonlight team measures product performance numerically and sets the direction for product development based on that data. I often analyze user feedback and sales data and think about ways to improve product perfection through this. In particular, we meet directly with customers to share opinions and continue to discuss ways to improve to create good indicators. The Corca LLM team is currently mainly talking about branding and promotional strategies. We focus on setting the direction of the product and establishing the brand image. We are devising strategies appropriate for the initial stage and considering how to effectively convey brand value. Q. What was the most impressive scene or episode while working at Corca? The most impressive moment was the workshop that took place last summer. It was an experience of moving to a new company-wide location, working and staying there together, and that in itself was really refreshing and memorable. Changing the location was refreshing, and better ideas came to mind in the new space. At the same time, I think it was a great help in healing and building teamwork with my teammates. It was especially special to have the entire company move together and experience this. It was a valuable time where I could get closer to my team members. I hope there will be another opportunity like this in the future, and I thought it would be great if the company grows further and one day I can go on work trips overseas😊 It feels like time flies so fast that already half a year has passed since the workshop I went to last summer! Like Ki-seong said, I hope the company can grow further and create even more great work opportunities in the future! Q. What do you think are the strengths of the current Corca team? I think the biggest strength of the Corca team is each individual’s sincerity and responsibility. It's really impressive to see everyone on the team feel a high sense of responsibility for their work and do their best. Also, everyone is great in terms of personality, so we get along without any problems, and I really like the atmosphere of respect and collaboration with each other. I believe that Corca's strong will to dedicate itself to the team and product is also one of Corca's greatest strengths. I think this is a team that naturally creates a good atmosphere. Q. Kisung, what does Corca look like a year from now? I expect that Corca, one year from now, will be fully on Moonlight's target sales track and well past the break-even point. We hope that the success of Moonlight will have a positive impact on the entire team and that other products will grow together and generate more sales. In particular, I believe that we will be able to become a more prosperous company next year based on this year's meaningful growth by steadily securing customers. I'm also looking forward to seeing the number of team members increase and we can move toward bigger goals together. Ki-seong, Corca’s reliable designer Q. What kind of influence do you want to have at Corca in the future? I have a strong desire to contribute more to the team rather than influence. Actually, when I first joined Korca, I was worried that there would be communication difficulties due to the age and generation gap, but fortunately, I feel like I am adapting well without any major problems. I think that the current design-related products are not completely stable, so I would like to play a role that can help the team not only in design but also in other areas. I would like to upgrade my capabilities so that I can provide greater value to the team, not just in product design but also in directing and management roles. Q. Who do you expect to join the Corca Product Team as a colleague? I think we need someone who has a good understanding of all products and can actively participate by distributing their time efficiently. Also, I think it would be a great help if there was someone who could provide meaningful advice without losing sight of the team's flow. Also, if you are someone who has an open mind, personality, and can communicate horizontally with team members, I think you will fit well with the atmosphere of Corca. Q. Is there anything you would like to say to prospective applicants to Korca as a Product Designer? If you are interested in AI, I think your experience at Corca will be more meaningful. Since we are planning and designing AI-centered services, if you have interest and understanding of AI, you will be able to create greater synergy in communication and work processes. Additionally, due to the nature of a startup, designers who are not limited to one role but can flexibly handle a variety of tasks as a multi-player are especially welcome. This was an interview with Corca’s fashionista, Kisung! I was really impressed by the deep affection and passion Kisung showed for his work. It was really cool to see him communicate with the team in a trendy and youthful way that belied his age! We hope that you will continue to play a strong role at Corca! Thank you for agreeing to the interview😊 Updated 2025.1.24

searchText: This is an interview conducted to inform the public about what the Corca Product Team does. Sunyoung Kim (HR Manager) and Minchae Kim (Product Manager) asked, and Jaeho Jeong (Product Lead) answered. What is the atmosphere and culture of the Corca Product Team? What does a Product Lead do and what concerns do they have? What does the product lead dream of for Corca? Q. Please introduce yourself! My name is Jaeho Jeong, and I joined Corca as a Product Manager in December of last year, and am currently in charge of Product Team Lead and LLM Native squad Lead! Q. Please tell us about what you do at Corca! Now mainly 0 to 1 work from product ideation to bringing it to market I'm doing it. Verify PMF If I'm doing it and it doesn't work, I pivot the product and repeat! What is PMF? Simply put, Product Market Fit is the compatibility between the product and the market. PMF is important because you have to release a product that is in demand in the market! Please tell us what kind of Trace app you are currently developing! Trace is a memo app based on LLM. This is it. It is not limited to a specific function, and if it is a notification, it is a notification, if it is a thought, it is a thought, if it is a to do, it is a to do. If you record freely, it will be systematically saved by LLM. It's okay. While existing memo apps only allow keyword-based searches, Trace allows context-based searches. It is an LLM-based memo app that has various functions, such as answering when you ask, "Why am I like this recently?" and automatically setting a reminder when you ask, "Set a reminder for 5 o'clock tomorrow!" Want to know more about trace? My own AI memo, trace, that makes everyday life easier Q. What capabilities or mindset do you think you need to do a good job as a Product Manager at Corca? Me too and when I see other people People who are not limited by role I think they accomplish a lot of things in a short amount of time. In Corca, there are many times when you have to do different things and speed up the pace. The most important thing is to have a mindset that allows you to do a variety of things. I think I did it! Q. When do you feel the fun and reward of work? Conversely, when is work difficult and difficult? As for the LLM Native squad, “Let’s work like a solo entrepreneur” This is the tone of our squad. I think it's fun to quickly implement what you've planned and see the outline of the results. I think I feel rewarded when my team members follow the principles I just mentioned, and when they break away from the existing method and adapt to a new method. I feel rewarded when I motivate them and they follow along diligently! On the other hand, in difficult and difficult times, there are times when I run at a fast pace and then slow down, and I sometimes feel frustrated at times like this. Q. What was the area where you grew the most while working as a Product Manager at Corca? I usually read a lot of product-related books and YouTube videos, and I feel like I've grown when I can understand the theories physically by trying things I only understood theoretically at Corca. The saying “Let’s work Lean” is famous in startups, but I think I have grown when I take it as meaning only, but when I actually work Lean and feel, ‘Ah, that’s what I meant’. Q. What is the most frequently talked about topic in Korca's LLM native squad these days? I think **“Conversation with Customers”** is what we talk about the most. If you don't consciously try to communicate with customers, you will be biased toward what you want, and you will end up creating products that are only conscious of your own tastes and preferences, not PMF's, so I think I'm talking about having more conversations with customers. Outside of work, the dress code for the year-end party was red, and I was impressed that Younghyun (CEO) came with red nail polish. If there is a dress code next time, I will prepare with passion! Q. Another big advantage is that there are no so-called old people, so teamwork works well. Q. Jaeho, what does Corca look like a year from now? When releasing the product again later A person who works sensibly and can also give advice to other team members I want to become this. I like to motivate people, and I want to be a person who can influence people who work with me to give more than 100% and give 120% and work in a product-oriented way! Q. Even if you initially think you can only do this, as you work, you will see many things. I hope there are people who can catch this and do it together! Q. Is there anything you would like to say to prospective applicants applying to Corca as a Product Lead? Corca is a place where you can grow as much as you want to grow, so if you are willing to grow, you can try many things! I'll be waiting🙌 Thank you, Jaeho, for taking the time to interview us despite your busy schedule ahead of the product launch! searchText: ‘Buddy program’ to help you adapt to new corkine. Introducing Corca’s onboarding culture, the ‘Buddy Program’. 2023-02-17 Ryu Ga-hyung (Product Manager) In this article, I would like to introduce the ‘Buddy Program’, a part of Corca’s onboarding culture! Corca has an Orcabot that helps with onboarding from the first day of employment. (If you are curious about Orcabot, please refer to the link below!) Hello Corca, Hello Orcabot Introducing the Corca onboarding bot, Orcabot Orcabot onboarding is conducted to get to know all team members by talking directly with them and completing quests together. But it's another thing to have the friendliest team member with whom you can talk about daily life and regularly ask how you are doing after joining Corca, whether you are adjusting well and whether you have any concerns, isn't it? Corca’s Buddy Program That’s how ‘(Buddy)’ started. The Buddy Program, which is conducted to help new team members who have joined Corca comfortably adapt, is a time when matched team members meet regularly and share various stories. Corca's culture with It is. By learning about Corca's culture and through the Buddy Program, new members can build rapport with Corca team members who are colleagues and whom they can rely on personally as mentors. Buddy matching criteria There was concern that if team members from the same job category were matched as buddies, we would definitely talk a lot about projects and work 😂 So, rather than talking about work, we are matching buddies from different occupations so that we can get to know each other more comfortably by talking about overall company life and each other. For example, those who joined the company as a Product Manager will be matched with an ML Engineer, those who joined the company as an ML Engineer will be matched with an Operation Manager, those who joined the company as a Dev Engineer will be matched with a Product Manager, and those who joined the company as a Data Scientist will be matched with a Dev Engineer! Existing team members who are already participating in the buddy program can restart the buddy program for new team members once the ongoing buddy program process is completed. 😉 So you can focus on one buddy at a time Any member who has been with Corca for more than 3 months can participate in the buddy program as an existing team member, regardless of age/experience, and everyone is happy to participate! Systematic buddy program implementation Are you curious about what we talk about during our multiple meetings with Buddies? For those who may be having difficulty, we are providing simple guidelines that are not required but can help 🥰 Check-in topic Day 1: On the day of joining, introduce the buddy program and say hello. After 1 week: Lunch to check if you have adapted well during the week, if there were any difficulties, and if you have any questions. After 1 month: Coffee chat time to discuss how you felt about working at Corca for a month, whether you had any questions, whether there are tasks you want to do/learn at Corca, etc. After 3 months: Follow-up meeting after the one-month check-in - Talk about project details, share dreams/goals, etc. and ask for help. It's time to talk about what we can give, but as a result of my personal participation, after meeting several times, an internal intimacy has built up, so simple questions such as 'Have you adapted well to Corca?', 'Are you having any difficulties?' Anything you two people have in common can be a topic of conversation in the buddy program! Lunch and coffee chat meal support Lunch, lunch support, coffee chat, cafe expenses. If you join the buddy program, of course, we support +. All you have to do is post it on the Slack channel as shown in the picture below and have a private time! Interviews with team members who participated in the buddy program I heard firsthand the stories of team members who participated in the buddy program. It was a really fun time to hear vivid reviews and episodes about how helpful the buddy program was 😆 Stories from existing team members Did the buddy program help you get closer to your new team members? Corgi found out that Buddy was dealing with similar concerns that he had when he first joined the company, and it served as an opportunity for them to talk better and become closer. He said that he wished he had had a buddy when he joined the company as well. Were there any memorable stories or episodes from the buddy program? Squirrel shared an interesting episode! He said he was impressed by the way the newly hired birdie ‘seriously imagined what she would be doing if she were Mansour’s daughter.’ 😂 These buddies are rumored to have played balance games for over 30 minutes since their first meeting. New team members’ stories Did the buddy program help you adapt to Corca and become closer to your teammates? In addition to the Corca project, I was able to hear stories about daily life, which helped me a lot in adapting. Alpaca said yes. It was good that the psychological distance from other team members was reduced. He first became friends with Buddy and told us about it! Were there any memorable stories or episodes from the buddy program? I found things in common and found people I knew in the same way. Bee says she started doing it while having a coffee chat with her buddy! What would you like to see added to make the buddy program more active? Flamingo, who has a lot of experience in various workplaces, shared his experience at his previous company and gave great feedback! After joining the company, it is mandatory to take turns eating with different teams every day for two weeks. Buddies diligently work together with their own team + other teams for a month for Coffee Chat. Rather than having a meal or coffee alone between a new employee and a buddy, the buddy takes the lead in meeting with other team members. Thank you again to all team members who participated in the interview. ! We introduced the buddy program that is in progress for new team members who have joined Corca. Below are photos taken and sent directly by Corca team members while conducting the buddy program! 🥰 Can you feel the harmonious and warm atmosphere of Corca? In order to create a buddy program that both existing and new team members can enjoy and be satisfied with, we actively reflect the feedback and suggestions that team members share, and we are creating Corca's culture together with our team members today. searchText: Is everyone eating? “Is everyone eating?” 2022-05-20 Choong-Hwan Han (MLOps Engineer) “Is everyone eating?” How often do you hear this? These are very kind and nice words, but strangely enough, I don't think it's easy to hear them often these days. In Corca, Orcabot asks twice a day. Are you all eating? “ ?” At 10:30 a.m., Orcabot is speaking kindly to me again today. Corca has a #bob channel on Slack. In response to the friendly questions Orcabot asks on this channel, what if you decide whether to eat or not, or express your desired menu using various emoticons? We are organizing groups of members who will eat together today. If you are curious about the development history of Orcabot, please also read Part 1 of Orcabot development history. Whether at school or work, there is a saying called ‘food friend.’ I think anyone who has ever wondered, ‘Who should I eat with today?’ will know the importance of ‘food friend.’ At Corca, you don't have to worry about friends because Orcabot lets team members know who they will eat with so that they can eat with a variety of people. What people want to eat every day may not be as good as MBTI, but it does seem to tell a lot about a person's tastes or mood that day. In that sense, having the same taste is a very convenient and good thing. 🥗 There are members who always eat salad for lunch 🍣 If you especially want to eat sushi or spicy octopus today, These are Corcans who are looking for members they want to work with on the #bob channel. 👀 Is there a reason why Corcas are so serious about food? This comes to mind, there is a saying that people who know a lot want to eat a lot. “ ” . I think the Corca people are very curious and passionate people, so they are sincere about their food! I think another reason is Corca’s generous food support and “ ”. One of Corca's benefits is that generous lunch and dinner meals are provided during working hours. In particular, at Corca, voluntary tech seminars are held in the evenings and some members also study, so there are quite a few members who work in the evenings. Therefore, there are many cases where we eat dinner together and work together instead of the typical company working hours of 9 to 6, and since both lunch and dinner are covered, it is a work environment where team members can eat more comfortably and work hard. I've seen large companies run in-house cafeterias to provide meals to their employees, or provide a certain amount of meal expenses in their salaries, but I was very surprised that they provide employees with a generous limit for one meal every time! I think that’s why Corcans enjoy ‘meal time’ with a joyful and happy heart and burn with passion during work hours. I think that mealtime has an important meaning, going beyond just eating something to satisfy hunger, it also allows you to build human bonds by sharing your concerns about work and life with the people you eat with. A friend of rice is a real friend 😆 . We are waiting for many people to become ‘Jjinchin’ who eat with Corcans.
